featured_reviews.name: Siddharth KV
featured_reviews.review_text:
VIIE presents its “2+2 abroad program” as a unique strategy developed by the institute. However, in reality, this is a standard credit transfer option already offered under Mumbai University, which any student from a Mumbai University–affiliated college can pursue if the foreign university accepts credits. This was not clearly communicated during admissions and felt misleading, especially considering the very high fees charged.

We were promised continuous support, including after moving abroad. In our experience, support began reducing even while we were still in India, and after relocating overseas, there was no meaningful support provided. Students had to manage academics, administrative processes, and settling in completely on their own.

VIIE appears to invest heavily in marketing and admissions outreach, but the actual delivery of promised services did not meet expectations. Several commitments discussed during the admission process were not followed through.

The faculty is knowledgeable and supportive, and they genuinely try to help students. Unfortunately, the management experience was extremely poor. From our experience, once the fees were paid, student support and accountability significantly reduced.

For anyone considering a 2+2 or international transfer program, it is strongly advisable to consult an independent education counsellor and fully understand all available options before committing to VIIE and paying the high fees.

Many positive reviews online do not reflect the experiences of students from our batch or seniors, and prospective students should do thorough research before making a decision.

Based on our experience, we would not recommend joining VIIE.

featured_reviews.name: Mansi Bait
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vidyalankar doesn’t even deserve to be called a college anymore. It’s a scam in the name of education. First, they suddenly hike the fees by 1–1.2 lakhs without even bothering to inform students or parents properly. No prior notice, no official communication, nothing. They just assume students are walking ATMs ready to pay anytime.

When I confronted the coordinator about this unfair hike, instead of giving a clear answer, he had the audacity to say “I was trying to reach you, but you didn’t pick up my calls or respond to my emails.” Excuse me? At first place, I never received a single call, message, or email from their side. They just make up lies to cover their mismanagement. And the cherry on top – the coordinator was unbelievably rude, arrogant, and completely uncooperative. Rather than helping, he spoke like he was doing us a favor by even existing.
So here’s the truth: Vidyalankar is not a college, it’s a well-polished scam factory. They loot money with hidden hikes, lie about communication, treat students like customers, and then fail to deliver when it comes to actual education or placements.

If you’re considering admission here – think twice. Or better, don’t think at all. Just run. Because once you step into Vidyalankar, all you’ll get is empty promises, rude staff, fake placements, and an endless hole in your pocket.

In short: Vidyalankar = Vidyaloot. 💸

My detailed review of DG RUPAREL college

Campus(4.5/5): It's a pretty good campus as the ground is good but gets worse during rainy season so be careful of that . A volleyball court which is good too. Pretty good greenery all over the campus.

Places to chill(3.5/5): total 3 places are there for a group to sit properly one is named as Sawali which is just beside junior college staff room another one is Rupangan which is on the other end of the ground which is decent in terms of chilling and the last one is the banyan tree which is near the back gate of the college . If anyone wishes to play games near these places beware as the watchmen comes to take your id card if he sees you playing .(Places to worry are Rupangan and Banyan tree , sawali is safe )

Attendance (4/5): Attendance they say is compulsory and all but don't listen to them they are just bluffing just try to attend maximum number of practicals and submissions on time even for 12th lecture Attendance is not there .

Facilities(2/5): Facilities are not so great here the toilets aren't well maintained for boys it's okay but for girls idk but I think it'll be not so good . Other than that the ground for playing and all yes you can play on the ground only after you get your id card and have to ask in the office if playing on ground is allowed or not just to be on the safer side the timings for that are 3-6 only in the afternoon(if you are not from the college sports team for those students) . Classrooms are below decent sometimes it's as the infrastructure and all the benches tables fans etc are really old .

Crowd(3/5): Everyone will have different crowd preferences and they can get their type of crowd for being frnds as all types of people are in the college as for the seniors my personal experience was that as long as you are profitable to them they are good to you once your purpose is done they won't recognise you and all so don't look up to them if you want to socialize be a volunteer during ganpati festival and all and then you can be with them if you want .

Faculty(1/5): Idk abt com and arts but for sci the faculty is not good as they don't care much abt students and are not cooperating might even make fun of you in cases to look cool and all for cs branch in jr college there are 3 teachers out of which 1 is very very good and also personally clears your doubts and all 2 is good but very strict abt things she clears your doubts helps you too but she is a bit strict and the 3rd one is the most hated as she doesn't know what she is doing a lot of times she seems clueless and teaching also not good

Festivals: No such things as festivals but there are days around dec I think which lasts for 5-6 different days like saree day tie day etc and no freshers for newcomers if you are hoping from college if you want freshers there is an unofficial one organised by student council which requires ₹1000 per person and tbh it's total waste of money they promise unlimited food but it finishes after the 3rd round and no trips from college side again unofficial trip by student council which requires around 17-18k per person

Boards perspective (4/5): Teachers manage your marks in the internals help you during practicals and if you manage to stay in their good looks you'll get out of marks in the internals just attend the practicals and clear all the submissions on time

Overall(3/5): a decent college if you want stress free attendance and internals during boards etc but if you want to live your college life like in the movies plzzz don't come in this college

Alongside technical courses, the curriculum includes extracurricular activities, soft skills training, and personality development sessions. In conclusion, Shri Bhaghubai Mafatlal Polytechnic College offers a well-rounded educational experience that prepares students for the challenges of the technical world. This is a formal complaint regarding the extremely poor and unprofessional support experienced during my spouse’s Online MBA program at NMIMS.
During the admission phase, the assigned counselor (Amita) was highly persistent in calling and following up for enrollment and fee payment. However, immediately after the payment of substantial fees, the level of support dropped significantly.
A critical issue arose when the exam registration link was not functioning. When we contacted the counselor for assistance, instead of providing guidance, she responded in an inappropriate and dismissive manner, stating:
"Main kyun aapko bataun? Aap kabhi mera phone uthate ho kya?"
Such a response is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about the professionalism and accountability expected from an institution of this stature.
To clarify:
• Students are not obligated to respond to repeated follow-up calls.
• However, once enrolled and fees are paid, it is the institution’s responsibility to ensure proper academic support and guidance.
• Denying or delaying support on personal grounds is highly unprofessional.
This experience reflects a concerning gap between the admission process and post-admission student support.
I urge NMIMS to:
Review the conduct of its counseling staff
Establish accountability in student support systems
Ensure that students receive timely and respectful assistance
If such issues are not addressed, it can significantly impact the trust and credibility of the institution.

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Nayar
featured_reviews.review_text:
What should have been a review has become a eulogy, as I was just informed that Dr. Sampat is no more.

A great principal isn’t just a leader; they are a force. They shape minds, build character, and leave a mark so deep that even years later, their words echo in your heart.

Dr. Urmi Sampat was that kind of principal. She wasn’t just an educator,she was an institution.

I still remember my first day at H.J. College. She stood at the gate in a crisp cream saree, radiating authority yet warmth. “What’s your name?” she asked. “Namrata  , and I’m am going to be the topper this year,” I replied with pride. She just laughed and said, “Go and sit yourself inside.” That was Dr. Sampat, no fuss, no unnecessary praise, just straight to the point. But in that moment, she acknowledged me. And with her, an acknowledgment always meant something.

She had this aura about her,if she caught you in the corridor, you’d hold your breath. If you were exhaling, you wouldn’t dare inhale again until she passed. That was the kind of presence she had. But beneath that formidable exterior was someone who truly believed in her students.

I remember struggling in my psychology paper. She called me in and asked, “What the hell have you done?” I admitted, “I had a blackout.” She didn’t let me off easily. “I don’t believe in blackouts, but I believe in you,” she said. And that belief changed me. I promised her I wouldn’t let her down. And when I topped my methods, she awarded me the prestigious Miss H.J Title of the year. That moment shaped my future in ways I didn’t even realise at the time.

One of the greatest compliments I’ve ever received came from her:

Personally, I see a junior Dr. Urmi Sampat in Namrata.
That comparison still humbles me.

Everything she taught me stayed with me. From my first lesson at NPKT to my journey as a teacher at Arya Vidya Mandir Bandra, to moving to Dubai , her words have never left me. The discipline, the passion, the high standards,they are woven into the way I lead today.

I wish I had the chance to say goodbye. But in a way, someone like her never truly leaves. Somewhere, I know she’s making sure everyone arrives on time, does their job well, and carries themselves with the grace and dignity she expected of us all.

Dr. Sampat, you were the epitome of grace, excellence, and discipline. They don’t make them like you anymore. I treasured you, and I always will.
Yours truly,
Namrata Simon Nayar

Avoid.

I studied B.Ed. here and it was a traumatic experience for me. I couldn't find a detail review about this place, so I will present a honest review.

Although the quality of teacher education in most institutes is pathetic, this is a terrible place to be in if one wants to become a good teacher. If you want to be a teacher who has empathy and kindness for children then this isn't a good place because you might be pushed to be otherwise.

Some points to keep in mind before taking admission here:
1. Most "teachers" are openly partial and discriminating. They get a FAT salary by the government and "train" those students who on average will get a paltry sum of salary and this perhaps give them a sense of excessive superiority. They are miserly tyrants as they will demand you to get their personal and unrelated errands (mazdoori) done for free. Don't know if the old principal who was unreachable to students except till the last day also treated them like that, but their nervousness infront of her betrayed a sign of incompetence.

2. In the name of discipline you will get to be treated as a slave. True discipline is about following the rules which is good but these people are not concerned about rules and openly flout it e.g. wrongly confining the original documents, forcing students to do things that they are not required to according to the actual curriculum they paid the fees for, and some of them won't bat an eye to give mean degrading remarks. They forget that there's a Constitution which has certain rules for state-funded institutes.

3. The NAAC grade is a joke which they got by accommodating the officers in an expensive Juhu hotel (as proudly but ignorantly revealed by one "teacher")

4. The senior clerk Aditi Nerurkar is a hateful mean bigot (and possibly a psychopath) who seems to have been given a free hand by the college to be as such.

5. Teaching skills before joining this course won't be much different after completing it, and of course it will be because what can you learn when people (most teachers) who don't have subject content knowledge nor could they understand education in so many years, lectures you for hours 6 days a week and makes you study from poor content ripped off online. But you can become a drama artist (or dancer) because that's what happens often on priority.

6. Internships are held like the horrible show of big boss contest without any checks and balances for how students behave towards each other, but it's of not much concern to them of course because it doesn't affect them. It's majorly a total waste of time and you'll get the same repetitive feedback so basically you aren't growing as a teacher.

The only "strong point" of this course is the class presentation / speech which is simply about blabbering stuffs. Sadly, there isn't any good that I find here except maybe punctuality and obediance? Not sure if this place has always been like that since 1969, if so then I can't imagine their contribution to society. Either way, I don't know why they always demand to be worshipped.

Office staff and non teaching staff is much more supportive than teaching staff. There are heavy regulations on what to wear and how to look and how to celebrate stuff.

Hostel not available for masters. Hostel facilities are okay. Surrounding areas are very costly for accommodation.

Campus is close to two stations, heavily crowded Wadala and moderately crowded Maunga.
